title: Velvet Gorse returns with Thornpipe
text:
Velvet Gorse, a financially motivated threat actor, used the Thornpipe backdoor in a series of intrusions this summer. Thornpipe exploits CVE-2099-41877, a path traversal flaw in Halvard Gateway appliances.

Velvet Gorse targeted water utilities in two regions. Operators should patch Halvard Gateway and review outbound connections.

title: Gorse Moth adds a second implant
text:
Gorse Moth, the group other vendors call Velvet Gorse, deployed Thornpipe against a freight broker in July.

We attribute the Murkbell credential stealer to Gorse Moth. Murkbell shares a packer and a staging server with earlier Thornpipe builds.

title: Saltmarsh Kettle activity against port operators
text:
Saltmarsh Kettle used the Quillstep loader to gain a foothold on harbour networks. Saltmarsh Kettle targeted port operators along the northern coast.

Based on code overlap and shared infrastructure, we attribute Murkbell to Saltmarsh Kettle.

title: Update: Thornpipe and Quillstep
text:
Thornpipe exploits CVE-2099-41877 in unpatched Halvard Gateway appliances. Saltmarsh Kettle continues to use Quillstep in new intrusions.

We found no evidence that Saltmarsh Kettle used Thornpipe.

title: Reedcutter and a new Quillstep operator
text:
Reedcutter, also tracked as Saltmarsh Kettle, targeted port operators in a phishing wave in September.

A second group, Ashen Lark, used Quillstep against a regional hospital network.
